design_space.current_assumption: 128/384/512 with three convs per block is the right shape.
design_space.why_material: Capacity is the binding constraint (F-003); shape sets both accuracy per epoch and seconds per epoch.

alternatives: fractional epochs tuned to the target
design_space.why_material: Time is linear in epochs; the best P1 cell sits at the grid edge.

design_space.current_assumption: airbench SGD with lookahead and triangular schedule.
alternatives: Muon on filters with SGD on biases and head
design_space.why_material: Muon cut CIFAR-10 epochs by about 20%.
Larger batches raise GPU efficiency but may need more epochs.
Low-resolution epochs cost about 44% fewer FLOPs.
Short budgets on CIFAR-100 may want less regularisation.
Compile cut CIFAR-10 time 14% at unchanged accuracy; it changes time, not accuracy.

hypotheses.proposition: The airbench96 shape reaches 75.3% below 10 epochs, or a nearby depth-3 shape reaches it at lower proxy time.
hypotheses.mechanism: Residual three-conv blocks raise accuracy per epoch enough that fewer epochs or fewer channels suffice.
hypotheses.prediction: Interpolated time to 75.3% below 9.3 s for some depth-3 shape.

hypotheses.proposition: Muon on conv filters reduces epochs to 75.3% by at least 10% at the selected shape.
hypotheses.mechanism: Orthogonalised updates equalise progress across filter directions.
hypotheses.prediction: Muon reaches the target in at least 10% fewer epochs at small Newton-Schulz overhead.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Proxy time at target within noise of SGD or worse.

hypotheses.proposition: Progressive resizing (24 or 24-28 px early, 32 px late) lowers proxy time by at least 5% at matched accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Early epochs learn coarse features at lower resolution and lower cost.
hypotheses.prediction: Time at target at least 5% lower.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Accuracy loss costs more epochs than the cheaper epochs save.

hypotheses.proposition: A larger batch (1536 or 2048) lowers proxy time at matched accuracy through higher GPU efficiency.
hypotheses.mechanism: Fewer, larger steps use the GPU better; airbench's decoupled parametrisation keeps step sizes comparable.
hypotheses.prediction: Seconds per epoch fall more than epochs to target rise.
hypotheses.disconfirming_result: Epochs to target rise by more than the per-epoch saving.

hypotheses.proposition: Weaker regularisation (label smoothing 0.1, lookahead off) suits short wide runs.
hypotheses.mechanism: Short budgets underfit rather than overfit, so regularisation slows convergence.
hypotheses.prediction: Accuracy at fixed epochs rises at least 0.2 pp.

hypotheses.proposition: torch.compile lowers seconds per epoch by at least 10% at unchanged accuracy.
hypotheses.mechanism: Kernel fusion removes elementwise and launch overhead.
hypotheses.prediction: Compiled proxy time at least 10% lower with accuracy within noise.

observations.statement: P1: the airbench96 shape reaches 75.37% single-view at 10 epochs (9.3 s local proxy, the best cell, at the grid edge); 2x two-conv width crosses at 13.7 epochs (12.0 s); narrow nets plateau below 75% (F-003).

omitted_dimensions.rationale: Fixed by RULES.md: single view, no TTA.
Fixed to GPU 1 by the team-lead directive; A100 timing is blocked (B-001, B-002).

probes.method: Depth-3 sweep: 128/384/512 at 6-10 epochs, 96/256/384 and 128/512/768 at 6, 8, 10 epochs, translate 2 vs 4 at 8 and 10 epochs; 5 seeds each.
probes.decision_rule: Select the shape and translate setting with the lowest interpolated proxy time to 75.3%.
probes.information_gain: Fixes the base before lever comparisons, which are only meaningful at the right shape.

probes.method: At the S3 base, run each lever at two epoch counts bracketing the target with 5 seeds, and interpolate proxy time to 75.3%.
probes.decision_rule: Adopt a lever if its interpolated proxy time is at least 3% lower than the base and its accuracy gain at fixed epochs exceeds two standard errors.
probes.information_gain: One pass decides four levers at the regime that matters.

probes.method: Run the climbed recipe eager and compiled, 5 seeds each.
probes.decision_rule: Use compile for final timing if it saves at least 5% with accuracy within noise.
probes.information_gain: Separates a systems gain from recipe gains.

question: Which levers lower local proxy time to a 75.3% single-view mean from the airbench96-shape base, and when does the climb saturate?
synthesis: Climb coordinate-wise from the P1 best cell: settle shape and budget first (S3), then levers at that shape (S4), then systems (S5), repeating S4 at the new optimum until no lever beats noise.
